results.summary:
How a Lighthouse Lens Works

• The original Fresnel lighthouse used a single thick piece of curved glass, which would have been very heavy.
• The Fresnel lighthouse used many thin glass rings and prisms arranged in a circle to bend light, resulting in a lens that is far lighter than a solid one.
• The lens turns slowly on a bed of liquid mercury or on ball bearings, driven by a clockwork motor.
• The time between flashes is a signature, indicating the location of the lighthouse.
• Some lighthouses use red or green panels to mark dangerous sectors, while others use white or colored lights to indicate safe course.

results.summary:
Lighthouses: A Short History of Light on the Coast

- Page title: Lighthouses: A Short History of Light on the Coast
- These are summaries of consecutive parts of one web page
- Part 1: Lighthouses have been used for navigation and safety for thousands of years
- The first lighthouse was built on the island of Pharos in Egypt around 3000 BC
- Over time, different types of lighthouses were developed, including open fires and coal beacons, and oil lamps with mirrors
- The Fresnel lens was invented in the 1820s and revolutionized lighthouse design
- Part 2: Lighthouses played a crucial role in maritime navigation
- The development of radio beacons and radar systems replaced the need for keepers
- GPS receivers became a reliable alternative to lighthouses
- Automation of lighthouses has been implemented in many countries

results.summary:
Lighthouse Summary

- Lighthouses have been used for navigation and warning ships of hazards since ancient times.
- The first lighthouse built was the Pharos of Alexandria in Egypt, which collapsed in 1323.
- The modern era of lighthouses began in the 18th century with the construction of the Eddystone Rocks lighthouse.
- The first lighthouse to use electric illumination was the South Foreland Lighthouse in 1875.
- The first lighthouse to use a gas burner was the Sumburgh Head lighthouse.
- The first lighthouse to use a solar-powered system was the Sumburgh Head lighthouse.
- The first practical installation of laser lights was at Point Danger lighthouse in Queensland.
- Lighthouse construction involves a rotating lens assembly to concentrate light.
- Lighthouse lantern rooms are typically glassed-in with metal muntins and have stormproof ventilators.
- Lighthouse towers can be painted in unique patterns to aid recognition.
- Lighthouses are used for various purposes such as aviation obstruction lighting, crib lighthouses, and day beacons.
- The use of lighthouses has been declining over time, but many groups are working to restore and save them.
- Lighthouse structures are being transferred to local governments and private non-profit groups through the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act of 2000.
